approved: National Vocational Education and Training Regulator (Charges) Amendment (Annual Registration Charge) Bill 2017
Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
This bill would change the legal basis of fees paid by training organisations to the national regulator, converting them into a tax.

It would amend the National Vocational Education and Training Regulator (Charges) Act 2012 to impose an annual registration charge as a tax, replacing fees collected under the National Vocational Education and Training Regulator Act 2011.
The charge would be limited to no more than the likely costs of the regulator's functions, and the Ministerial Council's agreement would be required on the amount.
Imposes an annual registration charge as a tax on registered training organisations and certain CRICOS providers.
Validates annual registration fees collected by the Australian Skills Quality Authority before 1 July 2017.
Requires the Ministerial Council's agreement on the amount of the charge.
Registered training organisations and certain CRICOS providers registered with the National VET Regulator.

The government introduced the National Vocational Education and Training Regulator Amendment (Annual Registration Charge) Bill 2017 and its companion bill to allow the Australian Skills Quality Authority to recover costs of compliance monitoring and intelligence analysis through an annual registration charge, replacing existing fees without additional financial impact on businesses.

The National Vocational Education and Training Regulator (Charges) Amendment (Annual Registration Charge) Bill 2017 is introduced to ensure ASQA is sufficiently resourced for compliance monitoring activities as a high-performing regulator.

Argued in support of technical bills clarifying that ASQA's annual registration charge is a tax under section 55 of the Constitution to remove legal risk, and cited a 2014 finding that the 10 largest vocational education providers received over $900 million in funding despite graduating only 4,181 students, about five per cent.

The speaker supported the bills to secure ASQA’s funding and restore the VET sector’s reputation, while criticising the government for cutting $2.8 billion from TAFE and reducing apprenticeships by 130,000 since 2013, and welcomed Professor Valerie Braithwaite’s review into ASQA and VET regulation.

The bills replace ASQA's annual registration fees with an annual registration charge, with an amendment ensuring the charge is set by a disallowable legislative instrument and limited to recovering ASQA's costs.
National Vocational Education and Training Regulator (Charges) Amendment (Annual Registration Charge) Act 2017
